meta.titre: Using the past perfect for an earlier past action

sections.contenu_markdown: When two things happen in the past, English needs a way to show which one happened FIRST: that job belongs to the past perfect.

items: Past participle forms of irregular verbs

sections.titre: Forming and using the past perfect
sections.contenu_markdown: The past perfect is formed with 'had' + past participle. It is used to show that an action was completed before another past action or before a stated past time, often with words like 'already', 'before', 'by the time'.

sections.enonce_markdown: Complete: Makanaky ... already ... his homework when I arrived (do).

etapes.action: Apply past perfect to the earlier action
etapes.justification: 'already' signals completion before the other past action.

etapes.action: Keep the later action in simple past

sections.conclusion_markdown: Makanaky had already done his homework when I arrived.

items.erreur_markdown: Using simple past for both actions when one clearly happened before the other.
items.pourquoi_faux: Without the past perfect, the sequence of the two past actions becomes ambiguous.
items.correction_markdown: Always use the past perfect for the earlier of two past actions when their order matters.

items.enonce_markdown: Complete: She ... (finish) her work before the meeting started.

items_markdown: Used for the earlier of two past actions, often with 'already', 'before'
